A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching algorithms, principal theoretical results, and identifiable appendix correspondences. The complete text, equations, algorithm displays, and tables support comparison.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results and proofs throughout the main text and Appendices A–E. Its conclusion identifies empirical evaluation as future work.

after.justification: v2 Appendix B reports original GPT2-large experiments on synthetic finance preferences and PKU-SafeRLHF, with measured win rates in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same private likelihood, square loss, policy reparameterizations, randomized response, and online exploration procedures. Label/index notation edits do not establish a different method; Appendix B implements existing objectives.

E1.justification: From no empirical datasets in v1, v2 adds training and evaluation on 1,697 synthetic financial-risk preference examples and 1,697 selected PKU-SafeRLHF safety preferences. Both experiments concern offline private alignment; online and adversarial-corruption settings remain theoretical.

E2.justification: Appendix B newly evaluates the MLE-type loss against the debiased log loss of Zhou et al. (2025a) and square loss of Zhou et al. (2025b), using the SFT policy as the win-rate reference. v1 discusses these alternatives theoretically but reports no empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces empirical protocols using GPT2-large, ε = 0.5, and llama3:70b judgments of win rate against SFT. PKU-SafeRLHF uses 1,442 preference-training examples, 85 validation examples, and 170 test prompts, with matched training conditions across losses and fixed A/B randomization. These evaluation designs have no counterparts in v1.

E4.justification: Neither version reports separate component ablations, sensitivity sweeps, corruption stress tests, or error/case analyses. Appendix B adds comparative performance evaluations of three objectives, without a distinct diagnostic or robustness study.

E5.justification: v2 introduces basic uncertainty reporting: five independent seeds and ± values for both experiments, with Table 5 explicitly identifying mean and standard deviation. Table 4 does not define its ± quantity. v1 contains no experimental repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports finance win rates of 65.2±4.3%, 65.8±5.6%, and 64.5±1.2% for MLE, debiased log, and square loss. Table 5 reports 61.45±2.81%, 61.95±2.50%, and 61.64±2.25% on PKU-SafeRLHF. The authors interpret both comparisons as similar practical performance; v1 has no empirical counterparts.

T1.justification: The principal bounds and fast-rate propositions are retained, with v1 Appendix E becoming v2 Appendix F. v2 adds approximate-realizability, log-linear-class, and history-dependent-corruption extensions in Remarks 4.6, 4.10, and 5.5. Appendix C.2 also corrects the Lemma 3.3 argument to use absolute bias bounds of 2α and 2c(ε)α in equations (4)–(5).

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and concluding claims retain the same substance: near-optimal private MLE, improved square-loss guarantees, and private/robust online alignment. The new empirical material supports these contributions without introducing a new central superiority claim.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies randomized-response and post-processing scope, explicitly identifies robust log-loss guarantees as an open problem, and qualifies the online optimality argument by distinguishing small and large β in Remark 5.6. It also interprets the new win rates and changes the empirical future direction from conducting experiments to expanding model scales and regimes.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents GPT-4o data generation, GPT2-large SFT through TRL, and SFT settings of learning rate 1e−5, batch size 8, and three epochs. It also specifies PKU filtering, selection seed 42, randomized-response privatization, β = 0.01, and χPO coefficient 0.25. These are newly documented experimental implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cheu et al. (2019), PKU-SafeRLHF, TRL, and Wu et al. (2025). Appendix A explicitly distinguishes Wu et al.'s private offline/online regularized results by their absence of corruption. The broader literature review and positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 removes duplicated preliminary text, makes local wording and notation edits, adds explanatory remarks and an impact statement, and adopts author-year citations. The experimental appendix shifts subsequent appendix letters and replaces the appendix contents listing, while the main narrative and section order remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the main text and references into a two-column conference layout with running headers and repositioned algorithm displays. It adds two theoretical comparison tables, a hyperparameter table, and two empirical result tables. Tables 1–2 summarize existing theoretical content; Tables 3–5 display new experimental material.

improvement.justification: Correcting v1's one-sided bias arguments in Appendix C.2 and clarifying optimality qualifications provide a modest gain in rigor and clarity. The new experiments add practical context but cover one model and privacy budget. Table 5's percentages also do not reconcile with the stated 850 binary comparisons per method, limiting confidence in that addition. The strongest quality gains therefore come from the theoretical corrections and clearer presentation.
